newsitem.title: NIGERIA: OAU expresses alarm over Africa's refugee crisis.
newsitem.headline: OAU expresses alarm over Africa's refugee crisis.

text.p: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) expressed alarm on Tuesday over the continent's flood of refugees, which it said numbered more than six million people.
A further 20 million people had been displaced by civil strife, it said in a report to a conference of African leaders' wives, gathered to discuss ways to promote peace in the region.
"The African refugee scene is increasingly becoming a permanent feature of our landscape," it declared.
"Despite concerted efforts, the problem of refugees, returnees and displaced persons is still very much with the OAU ...it has become alarming and a source of concern," it said.

The conference was held against the backdrop of civil war in Zaire, the stage for Africa's latest refugee crisis following a seven-month rebellion which threatens to topple embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko.
The Abuja conference, attended by around 20 wives of African leaders, is discussing how they can use their influence to bring peace to the world's poorest continent.
The OAU report also highlighted what it called a landmine "scourge" arising from war in Africa.
"More than 18 African countries have the scourge of anti-personnel mines," it said, listing among them Angola, Mozambique, Sudan, Somalia, Eritrea, Ethiopia and Rwanda.

Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha, whose wife Maryam Abacha initiated the talks, told the opening session on Monday that Africa must take its destiny in its hands by designing workable solutions to its numerous problems.
Dubbed "the first summit of African first ladies on peace," the talks will end on Wednesday with a declaration of what the women intend to do to achieve their goal.

A draft of the so-called "Abuja Declaration" obtained by Reuters said the women would arrange peace missions to conflict areas and help relief programmes for victims, complementing the efforts of international aid groups. They proposed to appoint a delegation to brief the OAU summit in Harare in June.

Delegates included first ladies from Namibia, Angola, Niger, Sierra Leone, Senegal, Gabon, Burundi, Equitorial Guinea, Gambia, Guinea, Chad, Zambia, Guinea Bissau, Ivory Coast, Ghana, Burkina Faso, Tanzania and the interim head of state of war-ravaged Liberia, Ruth Perry.
